jobs.title: Professional Geologist — Environmental Consulting
jobs.description:
Job description

Professional Geologist — Environmental Consulting

Company

Harris and Lee Environmental Sciences has provided environmental due diligence, site investigation, and remediation services to a diverse client base for over 30 years. We offer full-time, part-time, and contract opportunities.

Location

Northern California (candidate must reside in Northern California). Primary focus: greater Bay Area. All work is Remote except for site work and regulatory agency visits, which require local travel.

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced, detail-oriented Professional Geologist for Phase II–IV site investigations, monitoring, and remediation projects. This role includes hands-on fieldwork. The ideal candidate will coordinate/perform fieldwork, prepare technical reports, and communicate effectively with clients and regulators.

Key Responsibilities
Execute Phase II, III, and IV investigations, monitoring programs, and remediation activities
Perform hands-on fieldwork: sampling, logging, and site assessments
Provide oversight of field teams and subcontractors
Design sampling plans, oversee QA/QC, and ensure data integrity
Analyze geological and environmental data, interpret results, and prepare clear technical reports
Coordinate with clients, contractors, and regulatory agencies; represent the firm at site visits and meetings
Conduct ASTM E1527-compliant Phase I Environmental Site Assessments
Contribute to project planning, budgeting, and proposal development

Qualifications
Current, active California Professional Geologist license — mandatory
Must Reside in Northern California, Greater Bay Area -- mandatory
Proven experience with Phase II–IV investigations, monitoring, and remediation projects
Experience performing ASTM E1527-compliant Phase I ESAs
Demonstrated ability to perform hands-on fieldwork
Strong written and verbal communication and professional demeanor
Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
Ability to travel to local job sites throughout the Bay Area and Northern California
Relevant degree in geology, hydrogeology, or related field

Compensation
Salary commensurate with skills and experience.

How to Apply
Send resume and cover letter to:
Walter Beach
walt@hlenv.com
(415) 287-3007
﻿
Equal Opportunity Employer
Harris and Lee Environmental Sciences is committed to diversity and inclusion. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates.

jobs.title: Estimating & Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

San Diego based commercial services company is seeking an experienced Estimating & Project Coordinator
to join our growing team.

About The Position

The Estimating & Project Coordinator is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys staying organized, working with both office and field teams, and wants to build a career in paving, concrete, and construction estimating.

In this role, you’ll help keep projects moving by coordinating the information, documentation, schedules, and materials our estimating and field teams need to be successful. You’ll work closely with estimators, clients, supervisors, office staff, our yard, and field crews, giving you broad exposure to how paving and concrete projects move from an initial request through estimating and into the field.

This position is designed for someone who has strong coordination skills and is interested in developing deeper estimating knowledge over time. As you grow in the role, you’ll have opportunities to learn more about measurements, takeoffs, job costing, pricing, and proposal development.

In This Role, You Will

Coordinate next-day work orders and project information so field crews have the documentation and materials needed for scheduled work.
Prepare and organize project materials including photos, site maps, field forms, signs, cones, and other job-specific information.
Enter and maintain project information in Sage and support accurate records from the initial RFP through project completion.
Review incoming RFPs and help track bid opportunities, deadlines, project details, and missing information.
Support estimators by coordinating information for site visits, client meetings, measurements, photos, maps, and field observations.
Communicate project and scheduling information among clients, estimators, supervisors, office staff, the yard, and field crews.
Help ensure project completion information and follow-up are communicated accurately and on time.
Learn the fundamentals of paving and concrete estimating, including takeoffs, job costing, measurements, pricing, and proposals.
Take on additional estimating responsibilities as your knowledge and experience grow.

Requirements

About You

You’re organized, dependable, and someone who likes keeping a lot of moving pieces on track. You pay attention to details, follow through on commitments, and understand that getting accurate information to the right people at the right time can make a major difference in the success of a project.

You’re also comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where priorities can change. You enjoy collaborating with different teams and aren’t afraid to ask questions, learn new systems, or spend time in the field to better understand the work.

You may already have some exposure to construction, paving, concrete, estimating, or project coordination—or you may have strong operational coordination experience and want an opportunity to develop within the industry.

You’ll Bring

Typically requires at least 1 year of related experience with an applicable vocational or trade school certification desired.
Experience with construction, paving, concrete, estimating, project coordination, or similar operational support is preferred.
Strong organization, attention to detail, and time-management skills.
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
Basic computer and technology skills; experience with Microsoft Office and Sage is preferred.
The ability and willingness to work in both office and field environments.
Flexibility to adjust your schedule when project or operational needs require.
A willingness to learn, accept feedback, and continue developing your skills.
A valid California Driver’s License with an acceptable driving record for at least 3 years.

About Us

At Lot Commercial Property Services, we are a trusted leader in commercial property maintenance, partnering with some of the industry’s most respected property owners and managers. For nearly 40 years, we’ve built a strong reputation by delivering reliable maintenance services to shopping centers, office buildings, and other commercial buildings.

Our mission is to be the best place to work, where team members are empowered, supported, and given opportunities to grow in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.

About Benefits And Compensation

Our employees enjoy robust benefits including a generous company contribution to medical coverage and a 401k match. Additional benefits include dental, vision, accident coverage, and employer-sponsored mental health and wellness resources.

This position pays between $25.00 - $32.00 per hour
depending on experience.

All offers of employment are contingent upon successfully passing a pre-employment background check, drug screening, and physical endurance test relevant to the job requirements. We are an equal opportunity employer and consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. Equal Opportunity Employer D/F/M/V.

This employer participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your form i-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.

jobs.title: Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Amphenol Communications Solutions (ACS), a division of Amphenol Corporation, is a world leader in interconnect solutions for Communications, Mobile, RF, Optics, and Commercial electronics markets. Amphenol Corporation is one of the world’s largest designers and manufacturers of electrical, electronic and fiber optic connectors and interconnect systems, antennas, sensors and sensor-based products and coaxial and high-speed specialty cable. ACS has an expansive global presence in research and development, manufacturing, and sales. We design and manufacture a wide range of innovative connectors as well as cable assemblies for diverse applications including server, storage, data center, mobile, RF, networking, industrial, business equipment, and automotive.

Position:
Data Analyst

Location:
Etters, PA

Amphenol High Speed Products Group is the market leader for high-speed, high-bandwidth electrical connectors, cables, and systems for the Datacom/Telecom market (AI, ML, GPUs, Servers, Switches, Routers, Storage). Our products help to enable the artificial intelligence revolution by helping major Tier 1 Hyperscale Data Centers, their OEMs and break-out AI customers to innovate globally. Our global headquarters is in Nashua, NH and we have engineering, sales, and manufacturing locations globally. We are currently seeking detail-oriented, technically skilled Data Analysts to join our engineering team. We're hiring across experience levels, from junior to senior.

Responsibilities

The Data Analyst will support engineering teams by transforming raw operational data into reliable reporting and analysis that drives decision-making. Working alongside data scientists and software engineers, you will gather requirements, build and maintain dashboards, and improve the accuracy and consistency of data across multiple systems. Scope and level of ownership will be tailored to the candidate's experience.

Key Responsibilities

Collect, clean, and validate data from multiple engineering systems, reconciling inconsistencies across sources
Partner with engineering stakeholders to understand reporting needs and translate them into clear, actionable dashboards and reports
Build and maintain SQL queries and Python scripts to automate recurring data pulls and reduce manual reporting work
Conduct root-cause and trend analysis to surface issues and opportunities for improvement
Maintain documentation for data sources, definitions, and reporting logic so outputs are consistent and repeatable across the team
Perform data quality checks, flagging and resolving discrepancies before they reach stakeholders
For more senior candidates: lead requirements-gathering on complex initiatives and mentor junior analysts

Qualifications

A good candidate should have 3+ years of experience as a Data Analyst or in a similar analytics role; required experience will scale with the level of the role.

Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Analytics, or a related field required. MS preferred.
Comfort working with messy, real-world data, including cleaning, reconciling, and validating across multiple sources
Strong communication skills, able to gather requirements from non-technical stakeholders and explain findings clearly to mixed audiences
Experience mentoring or reviewing the work of others is a plus for more senior candidates

Technical Expertise

SQL skills, with the ability to write queries beyond pulling pre-built reports
Proficiency in Python (pandas or similar) for data cleaning, transformation, and automation
Experience with a BI/visualization tool (e.g., Tableau, Looker, Power BI)

Amphenol Corporation is proud of our reputation as an excellent employer. Our focus is to provide the highest level of support and responsiveness to both our employees and our customers, the world's largest technology companies. Amphenol Corporation offers the opportunity for career growth within a global organization. We believe that Amphenol Corporation is unique in that every employee, regardless of his or her position, has the ability to positively impact the business.

Amphenol is an “Equal Opportunity Employer” - Minority/Female/Disabled/Veteran/Sexual Orientation/Gender Identity/National Origin. For additional company information please visit our website at https://www.amphenol-cs.com/

jobs.title: Data Analyst - Disaster Recovery Cadre
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is adding experienced Cost Estimators to our Disaster Recovery team to support current and future disaster recovery operations across the United States.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world's most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential - join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Position Summary

As a Cost Estimator in Tetra Tech's Disaster Recovery Cadre, you will support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs by developing accurate, defensible, and well-documented cost estimates for infrastructure restoration, emergency work, and permanent work projects. You will evaluate damaged infrastructure, develop and validate project scopes, prepare cost estimates, and support funding eligibility determinations for public facilities and infrastructure.

This is an on-call, as-needed position supporting disaster recovery programs following hurricanes, floods, tornadoes, wildfires, earthquakes, and other federally declared disasters. Assignments may be remote, field-based, or hybrid depending on client needs and project requirements.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

Project Scoping and Damage Assessment

Support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs through project scoping, damage assessment, and cost estimating activities.
Support site inspections of damaged facilities and infrastructure to understand disaster-related damages, proposed repairs, and construction requirements.
Evaluate project scope, means and methods of construction, and restoration approaches.
Assist with the development and validation of disaster recovery project scopes.
Collaborate with applicants, engineers, architects, contractors, and program staff to define eligible work and project requirements.

Cost Estimating

Prepare conceptual, parametric, and detailed bottom-up cost estimates for disaster recovery projects.
Develop labor, equipment, materials, subcontractor, and general conditions cost estimates.
Estimate costs associated with repair, restoration, reconstruction, mitigation, and replacement projects.
Prepare cost analyses for roads, bridges, utilities, buildings, drainage systems, parks, and other public infrastructure.
Support development of FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF) analyses when required.
Develop estimate documentation that is clear, defensible, and suitable for audit and program review purposes.

Technical Review and Compliance

Review engineering reports, plans, specifications, contractor proposals, and construction cost documentation.
Evaluate project assumptions, quantities, unit costs, and estimating methodologies.
Apply knowledge of applicable construction standards, codes, and regulatory requirements.
Identify cost drivers, scope changes, and factors impacting project eligibility and funding.
Assist project teams with cost validation, reasonableness determinations, and documentation reviews.

Program Delivery Support

Provide technical estimating expertise to project managers, Public Assistance consultants, and applicant representatives.
Participate in project formulation meetings and recovery planning discussions.
Support Requests for Information (RFIs), technical reviews, appeals support, and other recovery program activities.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, architects, environmental specialists, grant professionals, and construction experts.
Maintain project records and supporting documentation in accordance with client and program requirements.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in construction estimating, engineering, architecture, construction management, infrastructure planning, or a related discipline.
Experience developing conceptual, parametric, and detailed cost estimates for infrastructure or facility projects.
Experience estimating labor, equipment, material, and construction costs.
Familiarity with modern construction practices, facility assessments, project scope development, and construction inspection activities.
Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Strong written and verbal communication abilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.
Ability to work independently and effectively under changing priorities and demanding schedules.
Ability and willingness to travel as needed for field assignments.
Valid driver's license.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Infrastructure Management, or a related field.
Professional Engineer (PE), Registered Architect (RA), Licensed Contractor, Certified Cost Professional (CCP), Certified Cost Estimator, or similar professional credential.
Experience using RSMeans, Xactimate, FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF), or other industry-standard estimating platforms.
Knowledge of FEMA Public Assistance regulations, policy, eligibility requirements, and the Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG).
Previous FEMA experience as a Cost Estimator, Program Delivery Manager, Site Inspector, Hazard Mitigation Specialist, Policy Advisor, or similar disaster recovery role.
Experience with roads, utilities, drainage systems, site development, vertical construction, or public infrastructure projects.
Experience supporting disaster recovery, grant-funded infrastructure programs, or public sector capital projects.

Physical Requirements

Ability to perform field inspections and site visits at disaster-impacted facilities and infrastructure when required by an assignment.
Ability to travel to client offices, applicant facilities, disaster recovery operation centers, and other project locations as needed.
Ability to perform computer-based estimating and technical review activities for extended periods during remote or office-based assignments.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

Work assignments may be performed remotely, in the field, or through a hybrid arrangement depending on client needs and project requirements.
Field assignments may take place in disaster-impacted communities and at damaged public facilities or infrastructure sites.
Work conditions and location may vary by assignment, including active disaster recovery operations and geographically dispersed project teams.

Additional Information

This is an on-call, as-needed cadre position. Work assignments are not guaranteed and depend on disaster declarations, contract awards, client needs, project requirements, qualifications, availability, and recovery program activations.
Acceptance of assignments is voluntary, and periods of inactivity between deployments may occur.
Assignment schedules may be flexible and may include periods of high-intensity workload during active recovery operations.
Some deployments may require extended travel or mobilization on short notice; other assignments may be fully remote.
Evening and weekend work may be required during surge events or active disaster recovery operations.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. With 30,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

Tetra Tech is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, marital or familial status, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law. Tetra Tech is a VEVRAA federal contractor and we request priority referral of veterans.

We invite applications from all interested parties.

Explore our open positions at https://www.tetratech.com/careers. Follow us on social media to learn more about our people, culture, and opportunities:

LinkedIn: @TetraTechCareers

X (Twitter): @TetraTechJobs

jobs.title: Business Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

The Business Data Analyst supports a business team’s ability to leverage data in support of business monitoring and decision management. Applies a range of analytics and data management techniques to generate accurate data and relevant insights, including the creation of visualizations and dashboards to optimize business decisions and outcomes.

Essential Functions

Engage with business teams to clarify needs and define business requirements for data analysis in support of business optimization and decision-making

Perform data exploration and analysis to identify and interpret trends and patterns in datasets

Create dashboards, visualizations, and reports to support business performance monitoring and stakeholders’ ability to be data-driven

Work collaboratively with the enterprise analytics & information management team to articulate business needs

Contribute to data inventory and stewardship efforts, including contributions to metadata management, data profiling, data quality remediation, and data cleansing

Perform research within the business area to determine the appropriate definition and logic for cataloging and modeling data within the analytics ecosystem

Perform user acceptance testing to confirm data output and capabilities meet business expectations and align to business processes

Troubleshoot data discrepancies and inconsistencies and partner with the enterprise analytics & Information management team to detect issues and automate resolutions

Maintain high standards and adhere to all enterprise policies and guidelines regarding data security and privacy, data management, data quality, and data governance; regard data as an enterprise asset that is to be protected and used both strategically and appropriately

Requirements

Job Specifications

Typically has the following skills or abilities:

Bachelor’s degree in statistics, analytics, mathematics, economics, computer science, or related functional area; or equivalent experience

2+ years of demonstrated data analytics experience including experience querying and analyzing operational and/or financial data, generating insights and communicating those effectively with colleagues and leaders

Experience building data queries using SQL in order to join, filter, cleanse, and aggregate data; understanding of how GUI-driven applications apply SQL concepts to do the same

Experience creating data visualizations/dashboards that highlight trends and patterns with the ability to monitor business performance against KPIs

Experience using data exploration and analysis platforms such as Cognos Analytics, Tableau, Power BI or similar

Familiarity with data modeling concepts and relational database structures

Ability to analyze and document business requirements, inclusive of needs and expectations

Effective written and verbal communication, presentation and analytical skills

Expert-level skills in Excel

For roles that are remote (i.e., Work From Home (WFM)) or hybrid (i.e., partial onsite at a VSP location and WFM), must demonstrate a high level of engagement in virtual environments, including maintaining camera presence during meetings to support effective communication and team alignment

Working Conditions

The working environment is generally favorable. Lighting and temperature are adequate, and there are no hazardous or unpleasant conditions caused by noise, dust, etc.

The above information in this description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job.

VSP Vision is an equal opportunity employer and gives consideration for employment to qualified applicants without regard to age, gender, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. We maintain a drug-free workplace and perform pre-employment substance abuse testing.

The compensation range for the role is listed below. Applicable salary ranges may differ across markets. Actual pay will be determined based on experience and other job-related factors permitted by law. As a part of the compensation package, this role may include eligible bonuses and commissions. For more information regarding iCare benefits, please click here .

Salary Description

$72,500 - $76,500

The Project Coordinator is responsible for supporting the Project Managers in job start-up, maintaining project files, maintaining all necessary documentation associated with the projects, and IDOT compliance.

Company Overview

With more than a century of exceptional work on our resume, William Charles Construction remains guided by the pursuit of excellence. Our “Do it Right the First Time” work ethic has been the cornerstone of our business philosophy since 1892. With our broad background in heavy civil construction, environmental management, and mining and materials production, we have the expertise to help our customers complete their most complex projects.

William Charles Construction is part of the MasTec Clean Energy & Infrastructure (CE&I) business segment. The CE&I segment generates over $4.5 billion in annual revenue, providing construction services across our renewables, industrial, infrastructure, and general building operating groups. Sustainability and safety are foundational to our culture and influence everything we do.

MasTec, a minority-owned Fortune 500 company, has shaped the construction industry for more than 90 years. With over 35,000 employees and 400 offices nationwide, we provide flexibility and career growth in dynamic work environments. Join one of the largest construction firms in the country (Engineering News-Record [ENR]: #1 in Power, #16 Top 50 Domestic Heavy Contractors, #13 Transportation Contractor).

Responsibilities

Prepare and circulate a list of current jobs.
Set up and maintain all job files on-line and hard copies.
Prepare pre-construction paperwork for new jobs.
Complete and submit job set up form and budget for grooving projects.
Review subcontract and submit paperwork to prime contractor for grooving projects.
Create purchase order and subcontract requisition forms and track progress between procurement and vendor.
Ensure that all required subcontractor paperwork is received and maintained.
Create and submit change orders.
Compute and process force accounts, back charges, and miscellaneous required billings.
Create and submit billings for grooving projects.
Track and submit subcontractor weekly certified payroll, monthly EEO, and quarterly PLA reports.

Qualifications

Associate's Degree in Accounting or Business Administration is helpful. A combination of education & experience will be considered in lieu of a degree.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

3 to 5 years of experience in business-related Accounting.
Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Outlook, Excel and Word.
Must be able to multi-task and work in a fast-paced environment.
Must have good oral and written communication skills.
Strong working knowledge of modern office procedures.

Compensation $23 - $27/hour, commensurate with experience.
401(k) with company match & Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)
Flexible spending account (Healthcare & Dependent care)

Diabetes Management, Telehealth Coverage, Prescription Drug Plan, Pet Insurance

Paid Time Off, Paid Holidays, Bereavement Leave
Military Leave, including Differential Pay and Benefits Continuation
Employee Assistance Program

Short and long-term disability, life insurance, and accidental death & dismemberment
Voluntary life insurance, accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity coverage
Emergency Travel Assistance Program
Group legal plan

jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for an On-Call Early Career Archaeological Field Technician
for our Albuquerque, New Mexico
office. Field duties would also extend into Texas.

Be involved in projects with our New Mexico Team
and be a part of a growing organization that meets our client’s objectives and solves their challenges.

At WSP, we are driven by inspiring the right people to be part of our future-focused business objectives. Our devotion to teamwork has allowed us to build communities and expand our skylines. Here at WSP, anything is within our reach- and yours as a WSP employee. Come join us and help shape the future!

Duties And Responsibilities

Conduct cultural resources fieldwork, reporting, and mitigation in support of pre-construction project design and engineering.
Help with all aspects of fieldwork, monitoring, data collection, inventory, analyses, and site form preparation.
Demonstrated commitment to keeping up-to-date in knowledge of current cultural resources management and Section 106 regulations and planning practices.

Talent is the essence of meeting our client’s objectives, goals and challenges. If this sounds like a fit for you, we’d love to have that first discussion of you joining our team.

Minimum Qualifications

0 to 3 years of experience working in the cultural resource management industry.
Knowledge of public and private sector requirements and practices for cultural resources surveys.
Ability to travel out of the immediate Albuquerque area over 2-10 days at a time, particularly in the SE NM area.
Ability to navigate and collect data using GPS equipment.
Good organizational skills, multi-tasking capabilities and attention to detail.
Competent interpersonal and communication skills when interacting with others and expressing ideas effectively and professionally to a technical and non-technical audience.
Basic proficiency with business writing, office automation and communication software, technology, and tools.

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated experience in the New Mexico BLM CFO region.
Familiarity with rules and regulations related to Section 106 of the Historic Preservation Act; and state and local environmental rules and regulations and related reporting requirements.
Bachelor’s Degree in Anthropology, Archaeology, Cultural Resources Management, or a related field (or equivalent experience meeting the Secretary of the Interior’s standards).
Demonstrated ability or progress toward being listed on federal and state cultural resource permits in New Mexico as Crew Chief.

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. Dedicated to serving local communities, we are engineers, planners, technical experts, strategic advisors and construction management professionals. WSP USA designs lasting solutions in the buildings, transportation, energy, water and environment markets. At WSP, we want to give our employees the challenges they seek to grow their careers and knowledge base. Your daily contributions to your team will be essential in meeting client objectives, goals and challenges. Are you ready to get started?

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is adding experienced Cost Estimators to our Disaster Recovery team to support current and future disaster recovery operations across the United States.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world's most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential - join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Position Summary

As a Cost Estimator in Tetra Tech's Disaster Recovery Cadre, you will support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs by developing accurate, defensible, and well-documented cost estimates for infrastructure restoration, emergency work, and permanent work projects. You will evaluate damaged infrastructure, develop and validate project scopes, prepare cost estimates, and support funding eligibility determinations for public facilities and infrastructure.

This is an on-call, as-needed position supporting disaster recovery programs following hurricanes, floods, tornadoes, wildfires, earthquakes, and other federally declared disasters. Assignments may be remote, field-based, or hybrid depending on client needs and project requirements.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

Project Scoping and Damage Assessment

Support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs through project scoping, damage assessment, and cost estimating activities.
Support site inspections of damaged facilities and infrastructure to understand disaster-related damages, proposed repairs, and construction requirements.
Evaluate project scope, means and methods of construction, and restoration approaches.
Assist with the development and validation of disaster recovery project scopes.
Collaborate with applicants, engineers, architects, contractors, and program staff to define eligible work and project requirements.

Cost Estimating

Prepare conceptual, parametric, and detailed bottom-up cost estimates for disaster recovery projects.
Develop labor, equipment, materials, subcontractor, and general conditions cost estimates.
Estimate costs associated with repair, restoration, reconstruction, mitigation, and replacement projects.
Prepare cost analyses for roads, bridges, utilities, buildings, drainage systems, parks, and other public infrastructure.
Support development of FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF) analyses when required.
Develop estimate documentation that is clear, defensible, and suitable for audit and program review purposes.

Technical Review and Compliance

Review engineering reports, plans, specifications, contractor proposals, and construction cost documentation.
Evaluate project assumptions, quantities, unit costs, and estimating methodologies.
Apply knowledge of applicable construction standards, codes, and regulatory requirements.
Identify cost drivers, scope changes, and factors impacting project eligibility and funding.
Assist project teams with cost validation, reasonableness determinations, and documentation reviews.

Program Delivery Support

Provide technical estimating expertise to project managers, Public Assistance consultants, and applicant representatives.
Participate in project formulation meetings and recovery planning discussions.
Support Requests for Information (RFIs), technical reviews, appeals support, and other recovery program activities.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, architects, environmental specialists, grant professionals, and construction experts.
Maintain project records and supporting documentation in accordance with client and program requirements.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in construction estimating, engineering, architecture, construction management, infrastructure planning, or a related discipline.
Experience developing conceptual, parametric, and detailed cost estimates for infrastructure or facility projects.
Experience estimating labor, equipment, material, and construction costs.
Familiarity with modern construction practices, facility assessments, project scope development, and construction inspection activities.
Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Strong written and verbal communication abilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.
Ability to work independently and effectively under changing priorities and demanding schedules.
Ability and willingness to travel as needed for field assignments.
Valid driver's license.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Infrastructure Management, or a related field.
Professional Engineer (PE), Registered Architect (RA), Licensed Contractor, Certified Cost Professional (CCP), Certified Cost Estimator, or similar professional credential.
Experience using RSMeans, Xactimate, FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF), or other industry-standard estimating platforms.
Knowledge of FEMA Public Assistance regulations, policy, eligibility requirements, and the Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG).
Previous FEMA experience as a Cost Estimator, Program Delivery Manager, Site Inspector, Hazard Mitigation Specialist, Policy Advisor, or similar disaster recovery role.
Experience with roads, utilities, drainage systems, site development, vertical construction, or public infrastructure projects.
Experience supporting disaster recovery, grant-funded infrastructure programs, or public sector capital projects.

Physical Requirements

Ability to perform field inspections and site visits at disaster-impacted facilities and infrastructure when required by an assignment.
Ability to travel to client offices, applicant facilities, disaster recovery operation centers, and other project locations as needed.
Ability to perform computer-based estimating and technical review activities for extended periods during remote or office-based assignments.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

Work assignments may be performed remotely, in the field, or through a hybrid arrangement depending on client needs and project requirements.
Field assignments may take place in disaster-impacted communities and at damaged public facilities or infrastructure sites.
Work conditions and location may vary by assignment, including active disaster recovery operations and geographically dispersed project teams.

Additional Information

This is an on-call, as-needed cadre position. Work assignments are not guaranteed and depend on disaster declarations, contract awards, client needs, project requirements, qualifications, availability, and recovery program activations.
Acceptance of assignments is voluntary, and periods of inactivity between deployments may occur.
Assignment schedules may be flexible and may include periods of high-intensity workload during active recovery operations.
Some deployments may require extended travel or mobilization on short notice; other assignments may be fully remote.
Evening and weekend work may be required during surge events or active disaster recovery operations.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. With 30,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

Tetra Tech is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, marital or familial status, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law. Tetra Tech is a VEVRAA federal contractor and we request priority referral of veterans.

We're hiring a Full-Time Project Coordinator/ Dispatch & Document Control Lead position at our Meridian Office!

Summary:

Support the office and project teams by coordinating inspections, managing project documents, tracking project information, and assisting with billing and administrative tasks for large industrial and construction projects. This role requires strong organization, communication, and multitasking skills in a fast-paced office environment.

Supervision Exercised
:

:

Utilize accounting systems, project management software, and Microsoft Office applications to track and maintain project data, documentation, labor hours, invoices, reports, and related records.
Create, organize, maintain, and distribute project files, reports, and administrative documentation in accordance with company policies, client requirements, and established procedures.
Coordinate and support billing activities by preparing invoices, reviewing project information for accuracy, monitoring project budgets and contractual requirements, and assisting with collections efforts when needed.
Process client payments by recording, depositing, and accurately applying funds to corresponding invoices within company accounting systems.
Serve as a point of contact for clients on billing-related matters, ensuring responsive, professional communication to resolve inquiries and support client satisfaction.
Perform quality control reviews of project documentation, reports, and billing packages to ensure accuracy, completeness, and compliance with company and client requirements.
Identify opportunities to improve administrative, scheduling, billing, and project support processes while providing general support to project managers and accounting personnel.
Perform other duties as assigned by management.

:

Certifications/License:

Qualifications (Knowledge/Abilities)
:

Strong experience with Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Excel, and Word.
Ability to learn new software systems and processes quickly.
Strong attention to detail with excellent organizational and multitasking skills.
Clear verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Basic understanding of accounting, billing, or financial processes is preferred.
Experience with project-based accounting or Ajera is a plus but not required.

Benefits:

Health Insurance
Dental Insurance
Vision Insurance
401(k) with Company Match
Paid Time Off (PTO)
Paid Holidays

:

Performing general physical activities related to the workplace such as talking, hearing, and seeing, especially where one must frequently convey detailed or important information quickly and accurately. Average hearing and conversational skills and the ability to properly receive information. Finger dexterity- the position uses repetitive movements of the wrists, fingers, and hands. Average visual abilities that allow one to inspect and prepare documents, manipulate tools, and operate office machinery. Position is highly sedentary and largely includes sitting, with occasional standing, walking, and bending over. May exert up to 10lbs occasionally.

The Research Project Coordinator serves as the link between administrative staff, fellows and faculty, and with peers and colleagues outside of these areas, ensuring high quality multi-direction communications between research stakeholders. The Estimating & Project Coordinator is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys staying organized, working with both office and field teams, and wants to build a career in paving, concrete, and construction estimating.

In this role, you’ll help keep projects moving by coordinating the information, documentation, schedules, and materials our estimating and field teams need to be successful. You’re also comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where priorities can change. You enjoy collaborating with different teams and aren’t afraid to ask questions, learn new systems, or spend time in the field to better understand the work.

The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is adding experienced Cost Estimators to our Disaster Recovery team to support current and future disaster recovery operations across the United States.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world's most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential - join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Position Summary

As a Cost Estimator in Tetra Tech's Disaster Recovery Cadre, you will support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs by developing accurate, defensible, and well-documented cost estimates for infrastructure restoration, emergency work, and permanent work projects. You will evaluate damaged infrastructure, develop and validate project scopes, prepare cost estimates, and support funding eligibility determinations for public facilities and infrastructure.

This is an on-call, as-needed position supporting disaster recovery programs following hurricanes, floods, tornadoes, wildfires, earthquakes, and other federally declared disasters. Assignments may be remote, field-based, or hybrid depending on client needs and project requirements.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

Project Scoping and Damage Assessment

Support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs through project scoping, damage assessment, and cost estimating activities.
Support site inspections of damaged facilities and infrastructure to understand disaster-related damages, proposed repairs, and construction requirements.
Evaluate project scope, means and methods of construction, and restoration approaches.
Assist with the development and validation of disaster recovery project scopes.
Collaborate with applicants, engineers, architects, contractors, and program staff to define eligible work and project requirements.

Cost Estimating

Prepare conceptual, parametric, and detailed bottom-up cost estimates for disaster recovery projects.
Develop labor, equipment, materials, subcontractor, and general conditions cost estimates.
Estimate costs associated with repair, restoration, reconstruction, mitigation, and replacement projects.
Prepare cost analyses for roads, bridges, utilities, buildings, drainage systems, parks, and other public infrastructure.
Support development of FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF) analyses when required.
Develop estimate documentation that is clear, defensible, and suitable for audit and program review purposes.

Technical Review and Compliance

Review engineering reports, plans, specifications, contractor proposals, and construction cost documentation.
Evaluate project assumptions, quantities, unit costs, and estimating methodologies.
Apply knowledge of applicable construction standards, codes, and regulatory requirements.
Identify cost drivers, scope changes, and factors impacting project eligibility and funding.
Assist project teams with cost validation, reasonableness determinations, and documentation reviews.

Program Delivery Support

Provide technical estimating expertise to project managers, Public Assistance consultants, and applicant representatives.
Participate in project formulation meetings and recovery planning discussions.
Support Requests for Information (RFIs), technical reviews, appeals support, and other recovery program activities.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, architects, environmental specialists, grant professionals, and construction experts.
Maintain project records and supporting documentation in accordance with client and program requirements.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in construction estimating, engineering, architecture, construction management, infrastructure planning, or a related discipline.
Experience developing conceptual, parametric, and detailed cost estimates for infrastructure or facility projects.
Experience estimating labor, equipment, material, and construction costs.
Familiarity with modern construction practices, facility assessments, project scope development, and construction inspection activities.
Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Strong written and verbal communication abilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.
Ability to work independently and effectively under changing priorities and demanding schedules.
Ability and willingness to travel as needed for field assignments.
Valid driver's license.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Infrastructure Management, or a related field.
Professional Engineer (PE), Registered Architect (RA), Licensed Contractor, Certified Cost Professional (CCP), Certified Cost Estimator, or similar professional credential.
Experience using RSMeans, Xactimate, FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF), or other industry-standard estimating platforms.
Knowledge of FEMA Public Assistance regulations, policy, eligibility requirements, and the Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG).
Previous FEMA experience as a Cost Estimator, Program Delivery Manager, Site Inspector, Hazard Mitigation Specialist, Policy Advisor, or similar disaster recovery role.
Experience with roads, utilities, drainage systems, site development, vertical construction, or public infrastructure projects.
Experience supporting disaster recovery, grant-funded infrastructure programs, or public sector capital projects.

Physical Requirements

Ability to perform field inspections and site visits at disaster-impacted facilities and infrastructure when required by an assignment.
Ability to travel to client offices, applicant facilities, disaster recovery operation centers, and other project locations as needed.
Ability to perform computer-based estimating and technical review activities for extended periods during remote or office-based assignments.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

Work assignments may be performed remotely, in the field, or through a hybrid arrangement depending on client needs and project requirements.
Field assignments may take place in disaster-impacted communities and at damaged public facilities or infrastructure sites.
Work conditions and location may vary by assignment, including active disaster recovery operations and geographically dispersed project teams.

Additional Information

This is an on-call, as-needed cadre position. Work assignments are not guaranteed and depend on disaster declarations, contract awards, client needs, project requirements, qualifications, availability, and recovery program activations.

Project Scoping and Damage Assessment

Support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs through project scoping, damage assessment, and cost estimating activities.
Support site inspections of damaged facilities and infrastructure to understand disaster-related damages, proposed repairs, and construction requirements.
Evaluate project scope, means and methods of construction, and restoration approaches.
Assist with the development and validation of disaster recovery project scopes.
Collaborate with applicants, engineers, architects, contractors, and program staff to define eligible work and project requirements.

Cost Estimating

Prepare conceptual, parametric, and detailed bottom-up cost estimates for disaster recovery projects.
Develop labor, equipment, materials, subcontractor, and general conditions cost estimates.
Estimate costs associated with repair, restoration, reconstruction, mitigation, and replacement projects.

Technical Review and Compliance

Apply knowledge of applicable construction standards, codes, and regulatory requirements.
Identify cost drivers, scope changes, and factors impacting project eligibility and funding.
Assist project teams with cost validation, reasonableness determinations, and documentation reviews.

Program Delivery Support

Provide technical estimating expertise to project managers, Public Assistance consultants, and applicant representatives.
Participate in project formulation meetings and recovery planning discussions.

Maintain project records and supporting documentation in accordance with client and program requirements.

Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

Ability to work independently and effectively under changing priorities and demanding schedules.

Valid driver's license.

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Infrastructure Management, or a related field.
Professional Engineer (PE), Registered Architect (RA), Licensed Contractor, Certified Cost Professional (CCP), Certified Cost Estimator, or similar professional credential.
Experience using RSMeans, Xactimate, FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF), or other industry-standard estimating platforms.
Knowledge of FEMA Public Assistance regulations, policy, eligibility requirements, and the Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG).
Previous FEMA experience as a Cost Estimator, Program Delivery Manager, Site Inspector, Hazard Mitigation Specialist, Policy Advisor, or similar disaster recovery role.
Experience with roads, utilities, drainage systems, site development, vertical construction, or public infrastructure projects.
Experience supporting disaster recovery, grant-funded infrastructure programs, or public sector capital projects.

Position Summary

As a Cost Estimator in Tetra Tech's Disaster Recovery Cadre, you will support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs by developing accurate, defensible, and well-documented cost estimates for infrastructure restoration, emergency work, and permanent work projects. You will evaluate damaged infrastructure, develop and validate project scopes, prepare cost estimates, and support funding eligibility determinations for public facilities and infrastructure.

This is an on-call, as-needed position supporting disaster recovery programs following hurricanes, floods, tornadoes, wildfires, earthquakes, and other federally declared disasters. Assignments may be remote, field-based, or hybrid depending on client needs and project requirements.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

Project Scoping and Damage Assessment

Support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs through project scoping, damage assessment, and cost estimating activities.
Support site inspections of damaged facilities and infrastructure to understand disaster-related damages, proposed repairs, and construction requirements.
Evaluate project scope, means and methods of construction, and restoration approaches.
Assist with the development and validation of disaster recovery project scopes.
Collaborate with applicants, engineers, architects, contractors, and program staff to define eligible work and project requirements.

Cost Estimating

Prepare conceptual, parametric, and detailed bottom-up cost estimates for disaster recovery projects.
Develop labor, equipment, materials, subcontractor, and general conditions cost estimates.
Estimate costs associated with repair, restoration, reconstruction, mitigation, and replacement projects.
Prepare cost analyses for roads, bridges, utilities, buildings, drainage systems, parks, and other public infrastructure.
Support development of FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF) analyses when required.
Develop estimate documentation that is clear, defensible, and suitable for audit and program review purposes.

Technical Review and Compliance

Review engineering reports, plans, specifications, contractor proposals, and construction cost documentation.
Evaluate project assumptions, quantities, unit costs, and estimating methodologies.
Apply knowledge of applicable construction standards, codes, and regulatory requirements.
Identify cost drivers, scope changes, and factors impacting project eligibility and funding.
Assist project teams with cost validation, reasonableness determinations, and documentation reviews.

Program Delivery Support

Provide technical estimating expertise to project managers, Public Assistance consultants, and applicant representatives.
Participate in project formulation meetings and recovery planning discussions.
Support Requests for Information (RFIs), technical reviews, appeals support, and other recovery program activities.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, architects, environmental specialists, grant professionals, and construction experts.
Maintain project records and supporting documentation in accordance with client and program requirements.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in construction estimating, engineering, architecture, construction management, infrastructure planning, or a related discipline.
Experience developing conceptual, parametric, and detailed cost estimates for infrastructure or facility projects.
Experience estimating labor, equipment, material, and construction costs.
Familiarity with modern construction practices, facility assessments, project scope development, and construction inspection activities.
Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Strong written and verbal communication abilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.
Ability to work independently and effectively under changing priorities and demanding schedules.
Ability and willingness to travel as needed for field assignments.
Valid driver's license.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Infrastructure Management, or a related field.
Professional Engineer (PE), Registered Architect (RA), Licensed Contractor, Certified Cost Professional (CCP), Certified Cost Estimator, or similar professional credential.
Experience using RSMeans, Xactimate, FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF), or other industry-standard estimating platforms.
Knowledge of FEMA Public Assistance regulations, policy, eligibility requirements, and the Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG).
Previous FEMA experience as a Cost Estimator, Program Delivery Manager, Site Inspector, Hazard Mitigation Specialist, Policy Advisor, or similar disaster recovery role.
Experience with roads, utilities, drainage systems, site development, vertical construction, or public infrastructure projects.
Experience supporting disaster recovery, grant-funded infrastructure programs, or public sector capital projects.

Physical Requirements

Ability to perform field inspections and site visits at disaster-impacted facilities and infrastructure when required by an assignment.
Ability to travel to client offices, applicant facilities, disaster recovery operation centers, and other project locations as needed.
Ability to perform computer-based estimating and technical review activities for extended periods during remote or office-based assignments.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

Work assignments may be performed remotely, in the field, or through a hybrid arrangement depending on client needs and project requirements.
Field assignments may take place in disaster-impacted communities and at damaged public facilities or infrastructure sites.
Work conditions and location may vary by assignment, including active disaster recovery operations and geographically dispersed project teams.

Additional Information

new_jobs.title: Business Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

The Business Data Analyst supports a business team’s ability to leverage data in support of business monitoring and decision management. Applies a range of analytics and data management techniques to generate accurate data and relevant insights, including the creation of visualizations and dashboards to optimize business decisions and outcomes.

Essential Functions

Engage with business teams to clarify needs and define business requirements for data analysis in support of business optimization and decision-making

Perform data exploration and analysis to identify and interpret trends and patterns in datasets

Create dashboards, visualizations, and reports to support business performance monitoring and stakeholders’ ability to be data-driven

Work collaboratively with the enterprise analytics & information management team to articulate business needs

Contribute to data inventory and stewardship efforts, including contributions to metadata management, data profiling, data quality remediation, and data cleansing

Perform research within the business area to determine the appropriate definition and logic for cataloging and modeling data within the analytics ecosystem

Perform user acceptance testing to confirm data output and capabilities meet business expectations and align to business processes

Troubleshoot data discrepancies and inconsistencies and partner with the enterprise analytics & Information management team to detect issues and automate resolutions

Maintain high standards and adhere to all enterprise policies and guidelines regarding data security and privacy, data management, data quality, and data governance; regard data as an enterprise asset that is to be protected and used both strategically and appropriately

Requirements

Job Specifications

Typically has the following skills or abilities:

Bachelor’s degree in statistics, analytics, mathematics, economics, computer science, or related functional area; or equivalent experience

2+ years of demonstrated data analytics experience including experience querying and analyzing operational and/or financial data, generating insights and communicating those effectively with colleagues and leaders

Experience building data queries using SQL in order to join, filter, cleanse, and aggregate data; understanding of how GUI-driven applications apply SQL concepts to do the same

Experience creating data visualizations/dashboards that highlight trends and patterns with the ability to monitor business performance against KPIs

Experience using data exploration and analysis platforms such as Cognos Analytics, Tableau, Power BI or similar

Familiarity with data modeling concepts and relational database structures

Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Position Summary

As a Cost Estimator in Tetra Tech's Disaster Recovery Cadre, you will support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs by developing accurate, defensible, and well-documented cost estimates for infrastructure restoration, emergency work, and permanent work projects. You will evaluate damaged infrastructure, develop and validate project scopes, prepare cost estimates, and support funding eligibility determinations for public facilities and infrastructure.

This is an on-call, as-needed position supporting disaster recovery programs following hurricanes, floods, tornadoes, wildfires, earthquakes, and other federally declared disasters. Assignments may be remote, field-based, or hybrid depending on client needs and project requirements.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

Project Scoping and Damage Assessment

Support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs through project scoping, damage assessment, and cost estimating activities.
Support site inspections of damaged facilities and infrastructure to understand disaster-related damages, proposed repairs, and construction requirements.
Evaluate project scope, means and methods of construction, and restoration approaches.
Assist with the development and validation of disaster recovery project scopes.
Collaborate with applicants, engineers, architects, contractors, and program staff to define eligible work and project requirements.

Cost Estimating

Prepare conceptual, parametric, and detailed bottom-up cost estimates for disaster recovery projects.
Develop labor, equipment, materials, subcontractor, and general conditions cost estimates.
Estimate costs associated with repair, restoration, reconstruction, mitigation, and replacement projects.
Prepare cost analyses for roads, bridges, utilities, buildings, drainage systems, parks, and other public infrastructure.
Support development of FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF) analyses when required.
Develop estimate documentation that is clear, defensible, and suitable for audit and program review purposes.

Technical Review and Compliance

Review engineering reports, plans, specifications, contractor proposals, and construction cost documentation.
Evaluate project assumptions, quantities, unit costs, and estimating methodologies.
Apply knowledge of applicable construction standards, codes, and regulatory requirements.
Identify cost drivers, scope changes, and factors impacting project eligibility and funding.
Assist project teams with cost validation, reasonableness determinations, and documentation reviews.

Program Delivery Support

Provide technical estimating expertise to project managers, Public Assistance consultants, and applicant representatives.
Participate in project formulation meetings and recovery planning discussions.
Support Requests for Information (RFIs), technical reviews, appeals support, and other recovery program activities.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, architects, environmental specialists, grant professionals, and construction experts.
Maintain project records and supporting documentation in accordance with client and program requirements.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in construction estimating, engineering, architecture, construction management, infrastructure planning, or a related discipline.
Experience developing conceptual, parametric, and detailed cost estimates for infrastructure or facility projects.
Experience estimating labor, equipment, material, and construction costs.
Familiarity with modern construction practices, facility assessments, project scope development, and construction inspection activities.
Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Strong written and verbal communication abilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.
Ability to work independently and effectively under changing priorities and demanding schedules.
Ability and willingness to travel as needed for field assignments.
Valid driver's license.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Infrastructure Management, or a related field.
Professional Engineer (PE), Registered Architect (RA), Licensed Contractor, Certified Cost Professional (CCP), Certified Cost Estimator, or similar professional credential.
Experience using RSMeans, Xactimate, FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF), or other industry-standard estimating platforms.
Knowledge of FEMA Public Assistance regulations, policy, eligibility requirements, and the Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG).
Previous FEMA experience as a Cost Estimator, Program Delivery Manager, Site Inspector, Hazard Mitigation Specialist, Policy Advisor, or similar disaster recovery role.
Experience with roads, utilities, drainage systems, site development, vertical construction, or public infrastructure projects.
Experience supporting disaster recovery, grant-funded infrastructure programs, or public sector capital projects.

Physical Requirements

Ability to perform field inspections and site visits at disaster-impacted facilities and infrastructure when required by an assignment.
Ability to travel to client offices, applicant facilities, disaster recovery operation centers, and other project locations as needed.
Ability to perform computer-based estimating and technical review activities for extended periods during remote or office-based assignments.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

Work assignments may be performed remotely, in the field, or through a hybrid arrangement depending on client needs and project requirements.
Field assignments may take place in disaster-impacted communities and at damaged public facilities or infrastructure sites.
Work conditions and location may vary by assignment, including active disaster recovery operations and geographically dispersed project teams.

Additional Information

This is an on-call, as-needed cadre position. Work assignments are not guaranteed and depend on disaster declarations, contract awards, client needs, project requirements, qualifications, availability, and recovery program activations.
Acceptance of assignments is voluntary, and periods of inactivity between deployments may occur.
Assignment schedules may be flexible and may include periods of high-intensity workload during active recovery operations.
Some deployments may require extended travel or mobilization on short notice; other assignments may be fully remote.
Evening and weekend work may be required during surge events or active disaster recovery operations.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. With 30,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

Tetra Tech is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, marital or familial status, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law. Tetra Tech is a VEVRAA federal contractor and we request priority referral of veterans.
